title: Faraday's induction
prompt: a coil of copper wire on a cardboard tube wired to a centre-zero galvanometer, with a bar magnet on a slider: push the magnet in and the needle kicks one way, pull it out and it kicks the other, push faster for a bigger kick, add more turns to the coil; see-through shows the magnetic field lines threading the coil and the induced current direction as moving dots in the wire
blurb: Move a bar magnet through a copper coil to reverse the galvanometer needle, then compare faster motion and more turns.
modelNotes: Teaching model with 12, 24 or 36 visible turns, a smooth illustrative flux profile, and quasistatic circuit resistance. Field lines and conventional-current dots are overlays, not physical parts or electron motion. Values illustrate Faraday's law rather than a calibrated apparatus.
